newsitem.title: THAILAND: Thai SEC reassures stock brokers on baht controls.
newsitem.headline: Thai SEC reassures stock brokers on baht controls.

text.p: Thailand's Securities and Exchange Commission (SEC) on Thursday said stock brokers in the local bourse should not be worried about latest currency control measures introduced by the central bank involving stocks trading.

Among other steps, the Bank of Thailand this week barred foreigners from repatriating baht funds made from share transactions. The move upset brokers and sidelined many foreign investors from the market.

"I think they should not be worried about the recent measures by the Bank of Thailand. Basically the measures have been discreet. Its just a group of people who are going to be affected by them and they are expected to be limited," SEC deputy secretary general Prasarn Trairatworakul told Reuters Financial Television in an interview.
"There has not been any substantial interference by the authorities in the stock market. So I think brokers should not be worried," he added.
He stressed that the new rule on local currency repatriation from stock deals was mainly aimed at preventing speculators from attacking the baht.

Another new measure announced by the Bank of Thailand on Tuesday required bank custodians not to accept transfers of borrowed and unpaid stocks from foreigners and non-resident investors selling Thai stocks must remit funds in foreign currencies only.

The central bank has also taken other control measures to cut off baht supplies from local sources to foreign baht speculators in dire need of the Thai unit to settle short baht positions following the latest mid-May speculative attack on the currency.
The Bank of Thailand launched the measures after the atack to punish speculators attacking its currency.
